# Test fixture provenance

Prefer deterministic synthetic files in temporary directories for exact-byte tests.
When valid media is necessary, record each checked-in fixture's generation command or
source URL, license, purpose, and expected result. Never commit personal media or
sensitive filesystem paths. Integration and E2E tests should agree on expected groups.

First-scan fixtures are generated by tests in temporary directories: short literal
byte strings (including deliberately invalid media with media extensions), empty files,
Unicode names, hardlinks, symlinks, FIFO, mode-restricted directories, and sparse files
for cancellation. All data is original synthetic test data; no decoding is performed
and no third-party media license is required. Linux-only invalid-byte names test safe
incomplete reporting. Test files are removed by TemporaryDirectory cleanup.

Media-size-summary uses `tests/summary_fixtures.py`: original literal bytes of 100,
100 and 50 bytes under selected extensions, plus 75 ignored bytes; expected summary is
3 paths / 250 logical bytes, or 4 / 350 with a hardlink. No image/audio decoding is
claimed. Integration/E2E add temporary links, FIFO, zero-byte files, real mode restrictions
and sparse files sized 2**32+1 and 2**32+2. Tests never read sparse payloads for snapshots.
A separate synthetic SQLite-row test covers aggregate arithmetic above 64-bit without
claiming such a filesystem fixture. Controlled mutation/I/O fault injection is labeled;
real paths and subprocesses still exercise the filesystem/CLI boundaries.

Relocation fixtures are original temporary literal bytes (`tests/move_fixtures.py`).
The shared tree contains two equal 100-byte media paths, a unique50-byte path and an
ignored100-byte text file. Real hardlinks, user/trusted xattrs, a synthetic valid POSIX
ACL encoding, NODUMP ioctl flags and disposable bind/tmpfs mounts test actual metadata
and containment. All mounts are unmounted in finally blocks. Publication/fsync/journal
failures are explicitly injected and checked against surviving bytes, not called real
disk-full or power-loss evidence. Signal tests launch the shipped main/argparse in a
subprocess and patch only a deterministic observation checkpoint to send real SIGINT/
SIGKILL; ordinary cross-volume E2E uses the actual `-m dup_media` entry point unpatched.
Linux CI requires privileges and ext4 plus distinct-device a second loop-mounted ext4 filesystem. The bounded
probe generates10,000 files of16 bytes (5,000 exact pairs) and a separate16-MiB pair;
no private media, decoder or downloaded samples. Results are not NAS throughput claims.


macOS relocation fixtures are original literal synthetic bytes, not decoded media.
Native libc creates disposable resource forks and arbitrary metadata attributes; APFS
image fixtures contain only generated test data and are detached after testing.
